title: Everyday object / 日常物件
input_provenance: AI-generated still-life of fictional worn canvas ballet slippers
workflow: Generated the input photograph first, edited that exact input, then refined only a few graphite pressure accents in the generated imprint.

before.prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural. Create an original, elegant editorial still-life photograph of a pair of softly worn light-ivory canvas ballet slippers with slender cotton ankle ties. These are flexible practice shoes with rounded toes, low openings, soft unstructured uppers and subtle stitching, not rigid pointe shoes. Show exactly two slippers, each with believable softly collapsed canvas and light signs of use: faint creases, slight fuzz along a seam, a little grey wear on one toe. Their pale warm ivory is sophisticated and restrained, not shiny white or pink satin.

Arrange the two slippers in a quiet asymmetrical diagonal on an uninterrupted deep pine-green matte surface. Seen nearly straight down, with slight dimensional soft light. Both shoes point generally toward the lower left; one toe is slightly farther forward and the other set a little behind, close together but not merged. The openings and complete silhouettes of both shoes remain visible. Long narrow cotton ties emerge from the shoes and make a few loose, natural intersecting arcs through the empty space above and beside them. They connect the composition gracefully without becoming a knot or decorative bow. Every tie is physically attached and logically continuous. The pair occupies about sixty percent of the portrait frame, with generous dark green breathing room around all edges. Keep the full shoes and the principal ribbon loops in frame.

Portrait 4:5. Independent arts-magazine object photography, tactile, understated, beautiful through the small evidence of use and the rhythm of the ties. Soft directional window light from upper left, gentle realistic shadows, clear fine canvas weave near the toes and stitching, believable slight differences between the two worn shoes. No human body parts, no hands, no mannequin feet, no flowers, no floorboards, no studio tools, no brand, no logo, no text, no watermark, no borders. Output only one full-frame color photograph.

after.initial_edit_prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Edit the supplied still-life photograph into one finished Soul Imprint artwork: the delicate graphite contact traces of the same two soft canvas ballet slippers and their cotton ties on quiet neutral-white paper. The photograph is the exact shape and composition authority. Preserve both complete shoe shapes, their relative size and positions, their direction, the one-forward-one-behind arrangement, visible openings, the ties' actual attachment points and their distinctive loose looping paths. Do not add a third shoe, separate the ties from the shoes, invent bows, reverse the shoes or reorganize the layout. Keep the original portrait 4:5 framing.

Translate the material into selective impressions, with believable differences between the edges, canvas, worn toe and ribbons. The raised binding around parts of the shoe openings and selected stitching lines should leave narrow, crisp dry graphite fragments. Canvas folds and worn toe surfaces leave sparse patches of fine cloth-grain deposits. The broad upper surfaces are largely untouched white, with only a few uneven mid-grey textile traces; do not fill each entire shoe with grey or render the interior dark. Several stretches of shoe perimeter should disappear gently into the paper so the eye completes the soft rounded shape. Preserve enough of the opening's rim and a few stitch marks to recognize each flexible slipper without conventional shaded 3D modeling.

The long ties should become elegant narrow ribbons of intermittent graphite, varying from a crisp woven edge to a fragile silvery remnant, then a short blank gap. Their loops remain in precisely the same places as in the reference. At crossings, maintain which tie goes over which so the composition remains physically comprehensible. Allow one small portion of a ribbon to leave a distinct woven-texture imprint; most of its path stays spare. No continuous vector outlines and no strand-by-strand pencil drawing. Favor a few decisive tactile details over overall completeness.

Remove the green backdrop entirely, replacing it with fresh luminous neutral-to-slightly-cool white thin kozo paper. The actual shoes are absent: only flattened transfer-like traces remain. No realistic object cast shadows, no beige canvas pigment, no photographic light gradient. A little paper fiber at close viewing and two or three almost invisible localized handling creases near a shoe boundary are sufficient; keep the large negative spaces calm. Dark graphite is limited to a few stitching/contact accents, with soft grey broken impressions and large genuinely empty regions. The composition should feel poised, tactile and intimate, with the rhythm of the ties and the evidence of wear giving it character.

Avoid simply making a desaturated low-opacity photo; avoid evenly sprinkled grain, a uniformly light sketch, complete pencil contouring, broad charcoal blobs, artificial antique stains, yellow paper, rigid pointe shoes, dirty feet, props or decorative flourishes. No text, signature, labels, frame, comparison layout or watermark. Output only the single white-paper artwork.

refinement.prompt: Refine this existing white-paper graphite imprint of two ballet slippers. Preserve exactly its composition, the two shoe shapes and openings, tie attachment points, all ribbon loops and crossings, portrait framing, white paper color and large unmarked areas. Make only one targeted improvement: add a small number of decisive pressure accents so this delicate artwork still reads at thumbnail size. Locally deepen a short arc of the nearer shoe's opening binding, a few stitch impressions at the forward toe, a small patch of woven canvas at the rear shoe's toe, and two ribbon-turn/crossing fragments. These selected accents should reach genuine dark graphite grey and contain beautifully sharp textile or stitch structure, interleaved with the existing soft impressions and blank gaps. A very small amount of sharper dry cloth grain can appear at the nearest toe. Keep the broad shoe uppers and interiors mostly white. Do not globally increase contrast, add ordinary pencil outlines, fill surfaces with grey, restore photographic shadows, add grit across the background, or change the ribbon paths. No added objects, words, border, frame or color. The result remains a spare, graceful tactile trace, now with a clear rhythm of sharp anchors and delicate absences.
